@@ -0,0 +1,73 @@
+---
+assignees:
+- claude-code
+depends_on:
+- 01M1MNWW4P14DK407XYSF22SMX
+- 01M1MNXY19R8HPEMNGF2WXB0G6
+- 01M1MP01P7SV7C2S0S8QZ0A60T
+position_column: todo
+position_ordinal: '8980'
+title: Download progress on stderr, and the verbose and quiet rules
+---
+## What
+
+cli-plan.md §5.7. The default profile is large, and nothing is on disk
+on a clean machine, so the first `acp-agent run "hello"` downloads
+gigabytes. A person who asks for a haiku and gets a silent terminal for
+ten minutes will conclude that the tool is broken. **Progress is not
+decoration here. It is the difference between working and appearing
+hung.**
+
+Router already does the work. `ResolutionProgress` carries the `phase`
+(`sizing`, `downloading`, `loading`, `ready`, `failed`), a `fraction`,
+and per-slot `bytesDownloaded` and `bytesTotal`, and
+`RoutedACPAgent.init` already takes `reporting: ResolutionProgress?`.
+This task passes one in and renders it.
+
+In `Sources/acp-agent/ProgressReporter.swift`, with the renderer the
+terminal spike chose:
+
+| Condition | stderr shows |
+|---|---|
+| stderr is a terminal | The phase, the slot, and a bar with the bytes. Then the running tool name on one line, rewritten in place. |
+| stderr is a pipe or a file | Nothing, until something fails. |
+| `--verbose` | The session events, one line each: the tool calls, the plan updates, the stop reason. In a pipe too. |
+| `--quiet` | Nothing but errors, in a terminal too. |
+
+The bar is drawn only for the resolution, and it is erased when the
+first answer chunk arrives. Nothing here touches stdout, so the §5.6
+byte-exact rule holds in every case.
+
+- [ ] Pass a `ResolutionProgress` into the agent construction
+- [ ] Render the phase, the slot and the bar, on stderr only
+- [ ] Erase the bar at the first answer chunk
+- [ ] `--verbose` and `--quiet`
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+
+- [ ] With stderr a terminal, a resolution draws a bar that advances.
+- [ ] With stderr a pipe, a successful default run writes zero bytes to
+      stderr.
+- [ ] `--verbose` writes one line per session event, in a pipe too.
+- [ ] `--quiet` writes nothing but errors, in a terminal too.
+- [ ] stdout is unchanged in every case.
+
+## Tests
+
+- [ ] `Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/ProgressReporterTests.swift`:
+      a scripted `ResolutionProgress` is advanced through `sizing`,
+      `downloading` and `ready`; the reporter's output holds the byte
+      counts, and it goes to the injected stderr handle only.
+- [ ] With a non-terminal destination the reporter writes zero bytes.
+- [ ] An integration test asserts that the bar never appears on stdout,
+      whatever the progress values.
+- [ ] `--verbose` and `--quiet` each get one test.
+- [ ] `swift test` passes.
+
+## Blocked by
+
+The Router change (`ResolutionProgress.fraction` and `.slots` public).
+Without it this task cannot read the numbers it must draw.
+
+## Workflow
+- Use `/tdd` — write failing tests first, then implement to make them pass.
\ No newline at end of file
